images.prompt:
Use case: compositing / architectural visualisation.
Asset: 16:9 architectural presentation hero for Bower, aimed at UK commercial retail asset managers.
Use reference image 1 as the authoritative GEOMETRY reference: it is one single six-bay timber pavilion shown from three viewpoints, not three different pavilions. Preserve its pointed timber arches, six supports, open circular crown and finely interwoven roof lattice. Use reference image 2 only for the trained climbing foliage character. Do not invent a different building.
Create a realistic architectural concept visualisation of this one Bower pavilion placed within a recognisable contemporary British outdoor shopping-centre square. Stone paving, two or three storey retail frontages with large glass windows, a café terrace on one edge, ordinary people shopping, meeting and sitting. Show the pavilion at human scale, approximately a small room rather than a whole plaza canopy. Preserve a wide clear circulation route around it and sightlines to shopfronts. Some discrete rooted climbers at the supports and partial leaf cover, enough that the actual timber geometry remains obvious. No mature garden, lawn, manor house, palace, woodland, floral tunnel, infinite promenade, or fantasy streetscape.
Composition: wide camera at human eye level, pavilion prominently right of centre occupying about 45% of image width, wholly visible including foundations/ground contact, shops visible around and behind it. The left third is a calmer area of paved retail square and shadowed shopfront, useful for a short slide title. Visitors and a few café tables demonstrate commercial context. Natural bright overcast UK daylight, restrained colours, credible materials and scale, editorial architecture photography quality. No exaggerated flowering, golden-hour spectacle, fisheye distortion or crowds.
Text: no text, logos, watermarks, captions or legible shop brand names. This is an illustrative proposal, not a documentary photograph of a completed project.

Use case: precise-object-edit / architectural visualisation. Create a second 16:9 view of the SAME proposed retail square and Bower pavilion shown in the first reference image. The second reference shows authoritative pavilion geometry from three views.
Keep the identity of the contemporary UK outdoor shopping centre, pale stone frontages, glass shops, light timber six-bay pointed arches, open crown, fine roof lattice and modest trained climbing leaves. Camera moves closer to the pavilion at ordinary seated-person eye level, looking diagonally through one opening across the central curved timber bench toward the shopfronts beyond. Show three or four ordinary visitors sitting, resting and meeting under the pavilion, relaxed natural poses, plus a couple of shoppers walking past outside. Show enough of the upper timber structure to identify Bower, but focus on the human-scale experience and on retail context visible through the openings. Nearby café chairs may be visible beyond. Keep wide clear pedestrian routes, credible root provision and paving.
Composition: pavilion opening and seated people occupy middle/right of frame; left quarter can include a shadowed timber support or quieter paved space for a short slide heading. Natural bright overcast UK daylight matching reference 1, restrained architectural photography, realistic materials and people.
Do not expand into a walkway, greenhouse, garden or canopy over the entire plaza. Do not add lawns, country house, lush flowers, water features, branded signs or fictitious readable text. No captions, lettering or watermark. This is a generated concept of proposed use, not an existing completed project.
